name: DG412CUE+
title: DG411, DG412, DG413: quad SPST analog switches, 44 V, ±4.5 V to ±20 V or +10 V to +30 V
summary: Four single-pole single-throw analog switches in one 16-pin package: normally closed in the DG411, normally open in the DG412, two of each in the DG413. On-resistance is 35 Ω maximum, matched to 3 Ω and flat to 4 Ω, and signals run rail to rail in both directions. They work from ±4.5 V to ±20 V or a single +10 V to +30 V, with a separate logic supply that sets TTL or CMOS input levels. Supply current is 0.0001 µA typical and charge injection 10 pC maximum.

circuits.title: Overvoltage protection with external blocking diodes
circuits.description: For systems where the supplies cannot be brought up in the order V+, VL, V-, then the logic inputs, one small signal diode goes in series with each supply lead: D1 from the V+ rail into the V+ pin, D2 from the V- pin out to the V- rail. A source Vg referred to ground drives the drain of one switch and the source is the output. The diodes cut the usable signal swing to 1 V inside each rail, leave on-resistance and leakage unchanged, and V+ to V- must still stay within 44 V.

circuits.title: Figure 2. Switching-time test circuit
circuits.description: Supplies of +15 V, -15 V and +5 V logic, GND at 0 V. A level VS on S1 passes to D1, which drives 300 Ω in parallel with 35 pF (fixture and stray capacitance counted in) to ground. IN1 is stepped from 0 V to +3 V with edges under 20 ns. tON runs from the 50 % point of the logic edge to the output reaching 0.9 of its final level; tOFF from the 50 % point of the opposite edge to the output falling to 0.9 of its level. A switch of opposite logic sense sees the inverted logic waveform; each input and switch is tested in turn.

circuits.title: Figure 3. DG413 break-before-make test circuit
circuits.description: A DG413 on +15 V, -15 V and +5 V logic. S1 and S2 both sit at +10 V; D1 and D2 each drive 300 Ω parallel with 35 pF to ground. One logic pulse, 0 V to +3 V, switches the normally open and normally closed channels together. tD is the time from one output falling to 0.9 of its level until the other output rises to 0.9 of its level, taken on both logic edges.

circuits.title: Figure 4. Charge-injection test circuit
circuits.description: A source VGEN with series resistance RGEN feeds S; D drives only the load capacitor CL to ground. Supplies are +15 V, -15 V and +5 V logic. IN is pulsed to +3 V; the step ΔVOUT left on CL as the switch turns on and off gives the injected charge, Q = ΔVOUT × CL. Which input and which polarity is used depends on the switch's logic sense. The charge-injection limits are measured with CL = 1.0 nF, VGEN = 0 V, RGEN = 0 Ω.
notes: Q = ΔVOUT × CL.

circuits.title: Figure 5. Off-isolation test circuit
circuits.description: A signal generator drives S over a shielded lead while IN holds the switch open (0 V or 2.4 V, by logic sense). D goes over a shielded lead to an analyzer and is loaded by RL to ground. V+ (+15 V) and V- (-15 V) each have a capacitor C to ground; VL is +5 V. The specified figure is measured with RL = 50 Ω, CL = 5 pF, f = 1 MHz.
notes: The S and D leads are shielded, the shields grounded.

circuits.title: Figure 6. Crosstalk test circuit
circuits.description: A 0 dBm signal generator drives S1 over a shielded lead; D1 is terminated in 50 Ω to ground. D2 goes to an analyzer, loaded by RL to ground, and S2 is left open. IN1 and IN2 are each set to 0 V or 2.4 V. V+ (+15 V) and V- (-15 V) each have a capacitor C to ground; VL is +5 V. The specified figure is measured with RL = 50 Ω, CL = 5 pF, f = 1 MHz.
notes: The S1, D1, IN1, IN2 and D2 leads are shielded, the shields grounded.

circuits.title: Figure 7. Channel off-capacitance test circuit
circuits.description: With the switch held open by IN (0 V or 2.4 V), a 1 MHz capacitance meter is switched between S and D, its other terminal on ground, to read CS(OFF) and CD(OFF). V+ (+15 V) and V- (-15 V) each have a capacitor C to ground; VL is +5 V.

circuits.title: Figure 8. Channel on-capacitance test circuit
circuits.description: With the switch closed by IN (0 V or 2.4 V), a 1 MHz capacitance meter between S and ground reads CD(ON) + CS(ON); D is left open. V+ (+15 V) and V- (-15 V) each have a capacitor C to ground; VL is +5 V.

operation.text: Each part holds four single-pole single-throw switches. In the DG411 all four are closed with logic 0 on their input; in the DG412 all four are open with logic 0 and close on logic 1. The DG413 pairs the two: switches 1 and 4 close on logic 1, switches 2 and 3 close on logic 0, and the DG413 alone carries a break-before-make figure, 25 ns typical.

A closed switch carries signal both ways equally. The on-resistance is 35 Ω maximum, matched to 3 Ω between channels and flat to within 4 Ω across the signal range; the signal may run from rail to rail. Charge injection is 10 pC maximum, off leakage under 5 nA at +85 °C, and the pins withstand 2000 V ESD minimum by Method 3015.7. tON is under 150 ns and tOFF under 100 ns. Power draw is 35 µW maximum. The process is a 44 V silicon-gate one.

The switches run from a bipolar supply of ±4.5 V to ±20 V or from one supply of +10 V to +30 V, with V- tied to 0 V in the single-supply case. Unequal supplies such as +24 V and -5 V also work. Supplies below ±15 V narrow the analog signal range, and at ±5 V switching takes twice as long or more.
VL sets the input threshold: +5 V gives TTL-compatible inputs, and VL tied to V+ gives CMOS-level inputs. The inputs are specified with VINH = 2.4 V and VINL = 0.8 V.

Supplies come up in the order V+, then VL, then V-, then the logic inputs, and no absolute maximum rating may be exceeded. Where that order cannot be guaranteed, one small signal diode in series with the V+ lead and one with the V- lead protect the part (circuit overvoltage-diodes). The diodes lower the usable analog range to 1 V inside each supply rail without changing on-resistance or leakage, and the V+ to V- difference must still not exceed 44 V.
The die substrate connects to V+. Internal diodes clamp any signal on S, D or IN that goes past V+ or V-; the current through them must stay within the maximum current rating.
The die measures 0.080 in (2.03 mm) by 0.097 in (2.46 mm) and holds 136 transistors. Dice are sold as DG41_C/D, with their specifications from the factory.

Source off, drain off and on leakage are tested on every part at the top of its rated temperature range; the +25 °C limits are set by correlation. Channel match and flatness hold only on bipolar supplies.
